decisions.title: Adopt a public decision register
decisions.summary: Keep project-shaping choices in a small machine-readable register.
decisions.rationale: The kit teaches agents to separate evidence from claims, so the repository should do the same for its own governance choices.
decisions.user_impact: Contributors can see why a behavior exists before proposing a new rule or adapter.

decisions.title: Adopt evidence-first agent behavior
decisions.summary: Generated agents must cite source IDs, preserve scope, and label local checks as structural-only.
decisions.rationale: Pine semantics change over time and often depend on chart context, account access, symbol data, and realtime behavior.
decisions.user_impact: A vibe coder gets a useful answer without hidden overclaims about compilation or trading safety.

decisions.title: Adapt release-note tracking into freshness review
decisions.summary: Use the Pine v6 official watchlist as a source-freshness review surface, not a stale task dump.
decisions.rationale: Some official changes are already represented by scoped rules, while others are only context until the project adds a matching surface.
decisions.user_impact: Readers can distinguish covered behavior from future review items without inheriting old internal work notes.

decisions.title: Reference manual TradingView checks only by hash
decisions.summary: Treat manual Pine Editor checks as stronger evidence only when a current file hash matches a dated record.
decisions.rationale: A Pine file can change while keeping the same name, so filename-based verification would be misleading.
decisions.user_impact: Users know exactly when an example has been manually checked and when it still needs TradingView.

decisions.title: Reject offline compilation claims
decisions.summary: Do not call local repository validation a Pine compile, non-repaint proof, security review, or profitability test.
decisions.rationale: The project does not ship TradingView's compiler, market data, brokerage context, or chart runtime.
decisions.user_impact: The public README stays honest and avoids giving traders false confidence.

decisions.title: Adapt public docs for people before internals
decisions.summary: Lead public documentation with user tasks, expected answer behavior, and evidence limits before repository internals.
decisions.rationale: The kit serves traders and AI coding users first; internal file maps are useful only after the reader knows what problem is solved.
decisions.user_impact: A new user can start with a Pine task instead of decoding repository architecture.

decisions.title: Adopt bilingual parity for public surfaces
decisions.summary: Keep English and Turkish README surfaces aligned in status, commands, warnings, and key links.
decisions.rationale: The project is community infrastructure and should not make one audience carry weaker safety language.
decisions.user_impact: Turkish and English readers receive the same operational truth.

decisions.title: Reference Verified Signal without adding runtime weight
decisions.summary: Use the visual system as public design guidance while keeping repository validation dependency-free.
decisions.rationale: Visual polish helps trust, but the core kit must remain usable with Git and Python standard library checks.
decisions.user_impact: The GitHub page can look deliberate without making validation harder to run.

decisions.title: Reject mandatory OpenAI or agent SDK runtime dependencies
decisions.summary: Do not require an API key, paid model account, or agent framework to consume the knowledge pack.
decisions.rationale: The kit is a portable public knowledge surface, not a hosted agent service.
decisions.user_impact: Community users can clone, inspect, and validate the project without signing into another platform.

decisions.title: Adapt adapters from one protocol
decisions.summary: Generate tool-specific instructions from the same protocol and catalog instead of maintaining independent claims.
decisions.rationale: Adapter drift would let one AI tool receive stronger or older Pine guidance than another.
decisions.user_impact: Supported tools behave consistently and contributors know where a factual change belongs.
